description: Somos Nova Protocol, un equipo apasionado por el espacio y los videojuegos. Estamos creando un juego cooperativo donde cada jugador asumirá un rol distinto dentro de una misión espacial y solo verá una parte del panorama. Con recursos limitados y decisiones que importan, el éxito dependerá de comunicarse y coordinarse. Queremos que la ingeniería espacial deje de ser abstracta y se aprenda jugando, en equipo.
summary:
Nova Protocol is a space management and engineering simulator that teaches, through play, how a real mission is built from scratch. It responds to a double problem: many regions export raw materials without refining them, so most of the value is created elsewhere, and many young people believe aerospace science is not for them.

The game answers with a playable value chain that follows the general flow of a space mission. Players first extract and smelt iron, copper and gold in the foundry, learning that value lies in processing. Those materials become the ship and its instruments, so the science objectives dictate the mission design, as in NASA's CMLs. Then two players cooperate to cross space: one plans the orbit while the other pilots through an asteroid field, which teaches orbital mechanics. On arrival, they use the instruments they built to analyze the planet.

Because each stage mirrors a real mission phase, from ground segment to flight to science, players see that engineers, chemists and programmers on the ground are as crucial as the astronauts. This breaks the myth that space science is out of reach for some communities, inspires STEM careers and raises awareness about industrializing natural resources, to move from raw-material exporters to technology creators. It also shows that local talent can be the engineering team behind a mission, not just the people dreaming of flying in it.
details:
Nova Protocol is a space management and engineering simulator in which one expedition is split into three phases linked by consequences, so what you do in one phase sets the conditions for the next. On the ground, you extract minerals and smelt them in a time-limited foundry to build the ship and its instruments. In space, two players cooperate in an asymmetric split screen: one plans the orbit while the other pilots through an asteroid field. On arrival, you use the instruments you built to analyze the planet, choosing what to test with incomplete information and living with the cost of being wrong. A final report grades the mission.

The core of the learning is process through repetition. Each stage is a short, replayable loop with clear feedback, so players internalize the chain of mining, processing, building, navigating and analyzing by doing it again and again, and seeded generation keeps runs comparable so improvement is visible. The chain shows that value lies in processing, that science objectives dictate mission design, as in NASA's CMLs, and that the ground segment is as crucial as the flight. This makes aerospace engineering feel reachable and inspires STEM careers, while giving the team a verifiable foundation to add planets, roles and modes without rewriting what exists.

The game was built with Godot 4.7 and typed GDScript, using native controls, procedural drawing, runtime-synthesized audio, and in-memory and ENet networking. It is versioned on GitHub and deployed on itch.io, so anyone can play it in the browser. Its creativity lies in the architecture: mechanics work like LEGO pieces, with generic parts in a reusable toolkit and the game only configuring them. Consequences chain into an economy, analysis is deduction under scarcity, and coordination between roles is itself the mechanic. To keep it fair and extensible, the team considered reuse before creation and determinism through seeded randomness.
dataRefs: Cubesat 101 - Basic Concepts and Processes for First-Time CubeSat Developers
